payload.rationale: With no prior trials, start from a strong default random forest: a moderate-depth ensemble captures the threshold-like sensor interactions typical of AI4I failure modes, while balanced_subsample class weighting suits the 3.4% positive rate and protects average precision under ranking-based evaluation.

Building on the incumbent forest, I test deeper trees with full feature subsampling (keeping the winning balanced_subsample weighting and more trees for stability), since AI4I failure modes hinge on multivariate interactions that the sqrt-limited, depth-8 trees may have underfit.

The large jump from t00 to t01 came from deeper trees and full feature sampling, which suits this dataset's threshold-style failure modes (torque/wear/speed interactions), so I extend that direction to the depth-20, all-features, 400-tree corner while keeping the winning balanced_subsample weighting.

The incumbent t02 sits at the boundary on every structural hyperparameter (trees, depth, leaves, features), so probing the only untouched axis — removing class re-weighting — at otherwise identical settings isolates whether weighting is contributing to average precision or whether unweighted fully grown trees rank the minority class even better.

The best trial (t03) showed that unweighted classes with deep, fully grown trees win by ~0.04 AP, so this perturbs only max_features (all → sqrt) to test whether feature decorrelation at the same 400-tree/depth-20/msl-1/none configuration further improves mean average precision.

The best random-forest config (t03) already sits at the search-space corner (400 trees, depth 20, leaf 1, max_features=all) with class_weight=none confirmed superior, so I probe the entirely unexplored logistic branch with interaction features and L1 selection, since AI4I failure rules (e.g., torque×speed power effects) are conjunctive and may be captured linearly once interactions are added.

Incumbent t03 sits at the capacity boundaries (depth 20, min_samples_leaf 1), so I probe one step of regularization (min_samples_leaf 2) around it while keeping the winning choices of max_features=all and class_weight=none, since the random-forest branch with unweighted classes clearly dominates logistic and balanced variants.

Building on the best trial (t06), I continue the improving trend in leaf regularization (msl 2 > 1) while keeping the winning settings of fully grown trees, all features, and no class weighting, which dominates the search history.

Holding the best-performing settings (400 trees, depth 20, max_features=all, no class weighting), I continue the monotonic improvement in min_samples_leaf (1→0.8194, 2→0.8227, 3→0.8240) by stepping to 4 to test whether extra leaf regularization further stabilizes AP on this imbalanced dataset.

The strong region is clearly RF with 400 trees, full depth, max_features=all, and no class weighting (class_weight=none beat balanced_subsample by ~4 AP points and max_features=all beat sqrt), and since min_samples_leaf 1–4 are statistically tied (0.8194–0.8240, fold std ~0.04), I probe msl=5 to test whether slightly stronger leaf regularization can push past the 0.8240 incumbent.

The unweighted 400-tree, all-features forest dominates and min_samples_leaf peaks at 3, so probing max_depth=16 (never tested in isolation) checks whether mildly pruned trees at this regularization level can beat the depth-20 optimum of 0.8240.

With the best configuration fixed except depth, reducing max_depth from 20 to 16 gave the best score (0.8246 vs 0.8240), so probing depth 14 tests whether the apparent depth sweet spot continues at shallower trees.

Depths 14-20 with min_samples_leaf=3 and max_features=all are within noise of each other with class_weight=none, so probing the shallower side at depth 12 tests whether less depth improves generalization on the small positive class.

AP improves monotonically as max_depth decreases from 20 to 12 at min_samples_leaf=3, so I probe the shallower depth 10 while holding the best-performing settings (n_estimators=400, max_features=all, class_weight=none) fixed.

AP improved monotonically as max_depth decreased from 20 to 10 (0.8240→0.8303) with min_samples_leaf=3, so probing depth 8 tests whether shallower trees continue to help while keeping the other best-performing settings (400 trees, max_features=all, no class weighting).
The depth sweep peaked at depth 10 (AP 0.8303) with min_samples_leaf=3, so I probe leaf=2 at that optimal depth to test whether slightly finer leaves improve the mean AP.

Probing the midpoint (depth 11) of the flat optimum between the two best configurations (depth 10: AP=0.8303, depth 12: AP=0.8270) while holding the confirmed-best settings of min_samples_leaf=3, max_features=all, and class_weight=none.

The depth sweep at leaf=3 shows a clear peak at depth 10 (0.8303) falling off by depth 8 (0.8220), so probing depth 9 pins down the optimum's peak, keeping the other best-performing settings (400 trees, all features, unweighted classes).

The response surface peaks around depth 9-10 with the depth-9/leaf-3 (0.8301) and depth-10/leaf-2 (0.8298) runs nearly matching the best (0.8303), so probing the unexplored depth-9/leaf-2 corner of that plateau with all features and no class weighting is the highest-expected-value local refinement.

The unweighted all-features forest plateaus at depth 9-10 (AP≈0.83), so I probe the last unexplored neighbor of the leader t18 by dropping min_samples_leaf to 1 while keeping the winning depth of 9, testing whether purer leaves at controlled depth add a final gain.

The surface peaks at shallow depths 9-10 with minimal leaf size (t19 depth9/leaf1 = 0.8309, t13 depth10/leaf3 = 0.8303), and depth 10 with leaf 1 is the highest-potential untried combination directly between those two best points, with no weighting and all features since class_weight=none and max_features=all clearly dominated.

Extends the min_samples_leaf=1 depth sweep upward from the current best (depth 10, leaf 1, AP=0.8327), since leaf-1 results improve with depth (0.8309 at 9 → 0.8327 at 10) while leaf-3 scores already peak near depth 9–10, and all other settings (400 trees, all features, no class weighting) are clearly dominant in the history.
placeholder

Probing the unexplored depth-12 cell with unpruned leaves (min_samples_leaf=1, max_features=all, class_weight=none), the winning settings, to test whether the depth-9–10 ridge extends past depth 11 (0.8306) given the gentle decline seen on the leaf-3 curve.

The top configurations (t19–t21, t13, t15, t17) are statistically tied within fold noise (σ≈0.038–0.040) around 0.830, all unexplored neighbors (depth 8 or 13 at min_samples_leaf=1, log2 features, min_samples_leaf≥4, balanced weights) project below the incumbent, and the logistic branch trails by >0.20 AP, so replicating the champion tightens the noisy estimate and maximizes expected final selection quality.

The search has converged on a plateau at max_depth 9–11 with max_features=all, class_weight=none, and 400 trees, so I extend the leaf-size sweep at the depth-10 optimum (leaf=1 leads by margins within fold noise) with the highest-prior untested neighbor, min_samples_leaf=4.

The peak region is depth≈10, min_samples_leaf=1, max_features=all, no class weighting, and since the 400-tree run is deterministic, a 300-tree forest at the same optimum re-rolls the ensemble averaging with the best chance of edging past AP=0.8327 while probing whether 400 trees are actually needed.

The winning region is unweighted 400-tree forests with max_features=all and min_samples_leaf=1, and the depth sweep at min_samples_leaf=1 (9→0.8309, 10→0.8327, 11→0.8306) leaves depth 8 as the only unmeasured point on this curve, a low-risk probe for the peak.

This is the only untried cell in the empirically strongest plateau (400 trees, depth 9–11, min_samples_leaf 1–2, max_features=all, class_weight=none) where all neighboring trials score ~0.83, so sampling it offers the best chance of beating the 0.8327 best while completing the local peak map.

The unweighted, fully-featured forest at depth 10 with leaf size 1 is the clear peak (AP 0.8327), so the only remaining unexplored axis at this optimum is max_features: probing log2 tests whether stronger per-split feature subsampling decorrelates trees enough to beat max_features="all" (which beat sqrt by ~0.027 at depth 20).

The champion plateau (400 trees, all features, unweighted, depth 9–11 with min_samples_leaf=1) is exhaustively sampled and differences there are within fold noise, so the next evaluation targets the last untested lever on the dominant branch — global "balanced" class weighting applied at the champion configuration — which has nonzero upside for ranking the rare 3.4% failure class where balanced_subsample's -0.04 hit was only measured at the unconstrained depth of 20.

The best region is a flat plateau (depth 9–11, min_samples_leaf=1, max_features=all, no class weighting) that is fully bracketed at n=400, so I sample the last untried plateau point, 350 trees, whose different ensemble has a real chance to edge past the incumbent 0.8327 given 400 is the cap.

The local grid at 400 trees (max_features=all, class_weight=none) is fully explored with a clear peak at depth 10 / min_samples_leaf 1, and AP rises with tree count (300→0.8312, 350→0.8318, 400→0.8327), so 380 trees at that peak configuration is the highest-expected-value untested point.

The history shows a clear optimum at max_features=all, class_weight=none, depth 10, leaf 1 (t20/t24/t32 all ≥0.8327), and since re-running exact configs is deterministic, I probe the untested 390-tree slot that interpolates the two best results (380 and 400 trees) to sample the top of the n_estimators plateau.

The depth-10 / min_samples_leaf-1 / max_features-all / unweighted forest region clearly dominates (0.8332–0.8333 at 380–390 trees, while class weighting, sqrt/log2 features, deeper trees, and the logistic branch all trail by wide margins), so I sample the one untested point in that optimal tree-count band, 385 estimators.

The depth response at min_samples_leaf=1 and max_features=all with no class weighting peaks at depth 10 (0.8327) and declines through 11–12, so testing the unexplored depth 13 completes the response curve in case performance recovers toward deeper trees, while retaining the other proven-optimal settings (400 trees, all features, class_weight=none) that put the search best at 0.8333.

The top of the search history forms a stable plateau around depth 10, min_samples_leaf 1, max_features all, and no class weighting (0.830–0.833 across trees counts 350–400), so I exploit that region with near-maximum tree count to keep fold variance low while nudging the ensemble size to avoid duplicating an already-evaluated point.

The search has converged to a noise-level plateau around depth 9–10, min_samples_leaf 1, max_features "all", class_weight "none", so I probe the only untested adjacency to the best trial (390 trees, depth 10) by testing depth 9 at the same tree count, where depth 9 already showed competitive means (~0.8301–0.8309) with the lowest fold variance in the region.

The search has converged on a clear RF optimum (depth 10, min_samples_leaf 1, all features, no weighting) where AP is tree-count-saturated and only fold-noise varies among 385–400 trees, so I sample the nearest untried tree count to the 400-tree ceiling to catch a favorable draw without duplicating an exact prior config.

The RF landscape has converged on depth 10, min_samples_leaf 1, max_features=all, class_weight=none, and the n_estimators response plateaus at 380–390 with the peak at 390 (AP=0.8333), so the untested interior point n_estimators=388 offers the highest expected AP with small residual uncertainty worth exploiting over clearly inferior logistic or differently-weighted branches.

The search has converged on depth 10, leaf size 1, all features, no class weighting with a shallow n_estimators peak around 388–392 (AP ≈ 0.833), so I sample this optimal region once more with n_estimators=392 to capture the plateau's best expected value before spending remaining trials.

All top trials cluster at max_features=all, class_weight=none, depth ~10, leaf=1 with 385–400 trees, and an untested n_estimators=391 sits between the two 0.8333 peaks (390 and 392), giving the highest chance of nudging past the current best.

The search has converged to a flat plateau at random_forest with max_depth=10, min_samples_leaf=1, max_features=all, class_weight=none, where identical configs reproduce deterministically and only n_estimators jitter (0.8322–0.8334) separates trials, so an untried nearby tree count keeps the dominant settings fixed while taking one more draw at the noise ceiling; alternatives (sqrt/log2 features, class weighting, depth 9/11–12, logistic) were all consistently worse.

The depth-10, min_samples_leaf=1, max_features=all, class_weight=none cell dominates the plateau near AP 0.833, and sampling it with the maximum 400 trees maximizes expected AP while minimizing fold variance.

All structural choices are settled (max_features=all, class_weight=none, min_samples_leaf=1, max_depth=10) and the deterministic tree-count response peaks at 388–392, so evaluating the untested n_estimators=389, bracketed by 0.8332 and 0.8333, is the highest-expected-value remaining probe.

The AP surface is flat and noise-dominated within the peak region, so I center the final config on its midpoint (depth 10, leaf 1, all features, no class weighting, ~390 trees) where the top scores of 0.8332–0.8334 were observed, maximizing expected AP over any remaining exploration.

The search has converged onto a noise-level plateau (AP ≈ 0.832–0.833, ±0.039) at max_depth≈10, min_samples_leaf=1, max_features=all, class_weight=none — alternatives (class weighting, feature subsampling, shallower/deeper trees, logistic) are clearly inferior — so I sample one more nearby untested point (n_estimators=393) to maximize the chance of matching or edging past the 0.8334 best.

Every structural dimension is conclusively mapped — depth 10, min_samples_leaf 1, max_features "all", class_weight "none" dominates (t30/t03/t29 vs. the plateau), while logistic lags by ~0.23 AP — so the only untested configurations are fresh n_estimators values inside the stable 385–395 plateau, where interpolating between neighbors 385 (0.8330) and 388 (0.8332) gives ~0.833 expected AP and a realistic chance of edging past the 0.8334 incumbent.

The search has fully converged on the flat plateau (max_depth 10, min_samples_leaf 1, max_features all, no weighting), where identical repeats reproduce exactly, so spending a trial on the untried n_estimators=397 — adjacent to the top-scoring cluster 388–392 (all ≥0.8332) — is the best fresh draw for surpassing the current 0.8334.

The search has decisively converged on unweighted forests with max_depth=10, min_samples_leaf=1, and max_features="all" (AP ~0.833 with peak draws at n_estimators≈389–393), so I spend the final evaluation on one untried tree count adjacent to that empirical peak to maximize the chance of edging past 0.8334.
